title: Ada and the Drop
premise: Financial-crimes investigator Odile Okonkwo, haunted by a botched witness extraction that left his informant dead, is pulled back in when the safe house he once ran is listed online with interior photos — proof someone inside is feeding information to the network he thought was dismantled. Tasked with extracting Ada Nwosu, a defector who may be deliberate bait dangled to lure him out, Odile must untangle which of his colleagues sold them out while staying one step ahead of assassins. The trail leads to his own mentor, whose laundering empire depends on silencing Ada. In the end, Odile sacrifices his career and nearly his life to get her testimony out, choosing survival with integrity over the corrupted inheritance his mentor offers him.
about_author: Emrys Joubert is the pen name of a former compliance analyst who spent a decade tracing money through shell companies before turning to fiction. They write thrillers about people trapped inside systems they helped build.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Insomniac and half-dissolved into desk work at the Financial Conduct Authority, Odile scrolls property listings at 3 a.m. and finds the old safe house for sale — every room photographed, including the hidden panic room only insiders knew existed. The emotional beat: dread reawakening; the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Clean Money
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. His supervisor assigns him, off-book, to extract Ada Nwosu, a defector from the Meridian syndicate hiding in that same house. Odile recognizes the assignment as either a trap or an apology for the incident two years ago. Beat: wary hope tangled with self-doubt as he takes the job no one else will touch.

chapters.title: Ada
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins: Ada's chapters trace her defection. She reveals she kept ledgers proving Meridian's laundering runs through legitimate banks — and that she contacted Odile specifically because of the incident. Beat: two damaged people circling each other, each wondering if the other is the bait.

chapters.title: Open House
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He stages a fake viewing to reach Ada, but the realtor is dead in the pantry and strangers are already touring the house. A running gunfight through the photographed rooms forces them out through the panic room's forgotten drain. Beat: adrenaline and the sick recognition that whoever listed the house wanted this meeting to happen.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. On the run, Ada explains 'the drop' — a nightly data dump from inside Meridian that has been leaking their movements. She believes it comes from within Odile's own agency. Beat: paranoia tightening; trust becomes the only currency, and neither can afford to spend it blindly.

chapters.title: Old Ghosts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. He confronts Marcus Hale, his mentor and the man who trained him, hunting the leak. Hale offers Odile a place in the quiet, comfortable corruption he's built — the inheritance of a lifetime, if Ada disappears. Beat: temptation laid bare; power offering itself as mercy.

chapters.title: Safe House, Unsafe
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The backup safe house is compromised before they arrive; Ada realizes the drop's source has been watching her since defection. She tests Odile by feeding him false information — and watches it reach Hale within hours. Beat: betrayal crystallizing, grief that the system itself is the traitor.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Cornered, Odile fakes Ada's death using the incident's own playbook — the exact failure that killed his last informant, now turned into a weapon. Hale buys it, but Odile must burn his identity, career, and clean record to do it. Beat: catharsis through self-destruction; redemption priced in everything he was.

chapters.title: Meridian
chapters.summary: Dual POV converging. Ada delivers her testimony to prosecutors while Odile walks into Meridian's headquarters wearing a wire, forcing Hale to confess on tape by pretending to accept his poisoned inheritance. Beat: climax — nerve, sacrifice, and the moment the corrupt empire hears its own voice recorded.

chapters.title: Daylight
chapters.summary: Odile's POV, coda with Ada. Months later: arrests ripple outward, Hale awaits trial, and Odile, unemployed and unburdened, sleeps through the night for the first time since the incident. Ada sends him a postcard from her new life. Beat: quiet resolution — survival without corruption, and rest finally earned.
